stops.name: Ostia, the last poverty by the sea
stops.campa: Keller comes home poor, without prospects, and takes a room in a boarding house at Ostia, lodged for nothing by an old friend of the Fiume days. The aristocrat has given everything away, as was always his way; only the fellowship of a few aviators, de Bernardi among them, remains to him. By the sea at the mouth of the Tiber the eagle of the Quarnaro grows still. He is thirty-seven, and the century that could not use him has left him at last on the shore, waiting for the road.

stops.name: Magliano Sabina, the car crash on the rainy road
stops.campa: On the night of 9 November 1929, in the rain on a road near Magliano Sabina in the Sabine hills, Keller's Fiat 525 swerves and goes off a bridge. The war-hero Vittorio Montiglio dies beside him; Keller too is killed, thirty-seven years old. So ends the eagle of Fiume, not in the air he loved but on the earth, at the roadside, in a crash like the ones that take so many of the atlas's seekers. The wildest spirit of the pirate-republic of poets is stopped at last by a wet Sabine curve.

stops.name: Il Vittoriale, buried on the Colle delle Arche beside the Comandante
stops.campa: By d'Annunzio's own wish Keller is carried to the Vittoriale degli Italiani above Lake Garda and buried on the Colle delle Arche, among the legionaries of Fiume, the place where the Comandante himself will one day lie. The poet who loved him as he wished to be loved gives his Segretario d'Azione a tomb of honour on the sacred hill. So the eagle who slept in a tree comes to rest in stone beside his commander, and the pirate-republic of poets, dissolved on the Quarnaro, is reunited in the earth of Gardone.
stops.quote: Egli era stato uno dei pochissimi che hanno saputo amarmi come io voglio essere amato.
stops.quote_source: Gabriele d'Annunzio, on the death of Guido Keller, 1929
